say: Thousands of songs use the same four chords.
Here is why, in one minute.
show: Thousands of songs use *the same four chords*. Here is why.

say: Start with the C major scale.
show: Start with the *C major scale*: seven notes.
C · D · E · F · G · A · B

say: Now build a chord on every note.
show: Build a chord on every note: *take one, skip one*.
Seven chords, all from the same seven notes.

say: Musicians number these chords, one to seven.
show: Number them *one to seven*: capitals for major, small for minor.

say: Three of them are the strongest.
Together, they hold every note of the scale.
show: *I, IV and V* hold every note of the scale between them.

say: and play them in this order.
show: Add vi, the minor one, and play: *I, V, vi, IV*.

say: In C, that is C, G, A minor, and F.
That shape is why it works.
show: Home, lift, a touch of sadness, and back home. *That shape is why it works.*

say: And it moves to any key.
In G, it is G, D, E minor, C.
show: It moves to any key. In G: *G, D, Em, C*.

say: and you can play thousands of songs, in any key.
show: Learn the numbers once, and play *thousands of songs* in any key.

say: That was one Fret key lesson.
There are more than two hundred and fifty, from your first note, all the way to jazz.
show: One *Fretkey* lesson. More than 250, from your first note to jazz.

say: and be among the first to play.
show: Fretkey is almost here. Follow *@fret.key* and be among the first to play.
